item.title: The Crimes We Refuse To Call Crimes
item.dc:creator: Priyasha Priyal Jena
item.description: When does bullying stop being a prank and become violence? This essay explores the hidden forms of cruelty society normalises in schools, the psychology of silence, and why some harms remain invisible simply because we refuse to call them crimes.

item.title: Money Can't Buy Happiness. But For Whom?
item.dc:creator: Priyasha Priyal Jena
item.description: The relationship between money and happiness is far more complex than popular sayings suggest. For some, wealth cannot solve loneliness or meaning. For others, money represents safety, stability, and survival itself.

item.title: Why Do We All Want To Look The Same?
item.dc:creator: Priyasha Priyal Jena
item.description: Beauty standards have always influenced how societies see us. But why do people with unique features so often feel pressured to become something more familiar? A reflection on conformity, pretty privilege, social media, and the psychology of wanting to belong.

item.description: We spend our lives chasing goals, building identities, and telling ourselves stories that make existence feel meaningful. But are we discovering purpose or creating it?
